parsed.summary: The file formalizes the Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture and proves it false. `quantitativeCompactnessCounterexample` gives a nonempty finite family of connected, bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with three properties: every member has ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3} eventually; every family-free host on n vertices satisfies e^16 ≤ C·n^21 for all n; and no member satisfies the compactness condition. The most important caveat is that the target `compactnessCounterexample_bigO` assumes `(1 : ℕ) = 0`, which is false, so that theorem is vacuous and certifies nothing. Theorem 1.1 is still fully captured by the quantitative theorem.

glossary.plain: A finite simple graph on vertex set Fin order.
The host G contains no member of the family as a subgraph (Mathlib `Free`, i.e. no injective copy).
ex(n, F): the maximum number of edges of an F-free graph on n labelled vertices.
glossary.note: The sup over an empty set would be 0, but the empty graph is always F-free when members have cycles.

glossary.plain: There exist F ∈ family and C > 0 with ex(n,F) ≤ C·ex(n, family) for all sufficiently large n.
Every finite nonempty family whose members all contain cycles is compact.
For every member F, eventually c·n^{4/3} ≤ ex(n,F).
glossary.note: Uses one c for all members; this is equivalent for a finite family.

lean_claims.plain: The compactness conjecture (corrected form) is false.

There exist a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, and c, C > 0 such that: (i) for each F ∈ F, eventually ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3}; (ii) for all n and every F-free host on n vertices, e(G)^16 ≤ C·n^21, hence ex(n,F)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for all n; (iii) 21/16 = 4/3 − 1/48; (iv) F is not compact; and (v) the conjecture fails.
Under the false hypothesis 1 = 0 in ℕ: such a family exists with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}). The theorem is vacuous.

paper_claims.plain: There is a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}) and ex(n,F) = Ω(n^{4/3}) for each F ∈ F; hence no member satisfies (1).
There is a connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all large n.

coverage.why: The upper bound holds for all n with an explicit power inequality, the lower constant is uniform, and non-compactness is included.
Vacuous because of the false hypothesis 1 = 0.
